question: The invocation restates Purpose, Owns, Isolation strategy and Overview from PRD v2 and the citation touch (H11) moves this file's source citations later. How do the restated sentences cite their sources?

options.label: restated text cites PRD v2 and the ADRs; untouched citations wait for H11
options.consequence: Each rewritten sentence names the PRD v2 section or ADR it comes from. The header's Sources field (PRD 1 and Update 1 paths) and the Phase Plan keep their references, so H11's cites-superseded condition still holds and H11 moves them.

options.label: restated text keeps the old 'from the PRD' markers
options.consequence: The Overview would say the accounts come 'from the PRD', meaning PRD 1, for data PRD v2 Demo accounts now defines with time zones, and H11 would rewrite sentences it did not author.

options.label: restated text carries no citation
options.consequence: Nothing is wrong between steps, but a planner loses the pointer from the database, the rooms and the time zone to the PRD v2 section that requires them.

chosen: restated text cites PRD v2 and the ADRs; untouched citations wait for H11
why: A citation names where its sentence comes from, and every restated sentence comes from PRD v2 (Constraints, Team and delivery, Demo accounts, Rooms, US-4 to US-6, AC-2.5) or from ADR-001 and ADR-002. S08 took the same rule for the root (DEC-067), so the two specs read alike. The Sources field is left for H11 as the invocation and the intake record (Sources and Scope) say.

question: How does simple-login.backend's Purpose, in its own file and in the embedded summary in hsdd/spec/simple-login.md, gain the pre-loaded rooms, the bookings, the time zone and PostgreSQL 17?

options.label: one sentence naming the profile's time zone and the room bookings kept in PostgreSQL 17
options.consequence: Purpose reads: authenticate built-in users and serve over HTTP the signed-in user's profile with their time zone and the bookings of the pre-loaded meeting rooms (each room's bookings on a date, booking a room, the user's own bookings, cancelling one), keeping the bookings in PostgreSQL 17. Still one responsibility, the service behind the product's API, now with its four booking uses.

options.label: a generic sentence
options.consequence: 'serve the product's API' survives the next PRD, but a planner learns nothing from it, and the node's Purpose would no longer say what it authenticates or keeps.

options.label: keep the old Purpose; let the Overview carry booking
options.consequence: Smallest change, but the parent's embedded summary, which has no Overview, would still describe a sign-in and profile service, and the invocation names Purpose.

chosen: one sentence naming the profile's time zone and the room bookings kept in PostgreSQL 17
why: The invocation names Purpose for the rooms, bookings, the time zone and the database. PRD v2 Team and delivery keeps the whole service and the database with the backend developer, so booking is the same owner's responsibility, not a second one; the sentence keeps the old Purpose's form (what it authenticates and serves, over HTTP) and lists the four uses as PRD v2 US-4 to US-6 name them. Endpoints and the Docker Compose service go to Owns, which is where the old header named endpoints.

question: What does simple-login.backend's Owns gain, in its own file and in the embedded summary: the booking endpoints by path or by contract, and the Docker Compose service with or without its file and a fixed location?

options.label: endpoints by path; the Compose service and its file, location left to the plan
options.consequence: Owns adds the accounts' time zones, the pre-loaded rooms, the bookings, the PostgreSQL 17 database that keeps them, its Docker Compose service and that service's Compose file, and GET /api/rooms, GET /api/me/bookings, POST /api/bookings and DELETE /api/bookings/{id} beside the two auth paths. If booking-api, still draft, renames a path before it is stable, this line needs another touch.

options.label: endpoints as 'booking-api's endpoints'
options.consequence: Survives a path change in the draft contract, but breaks the line's form (the auth endpoints are named by path), and a contract name in Owns becomes one more citation each later version bump must move.

options.label: pin the Compose file under backend/
options.consequence: Ownership follows from the existing `backend/` entry with no new item, but fixes a layout choice that the plan owner makes, before H14 has weighed how simple-login.integration's root scripts start the database.

chosen: endpoints by path; the Compose service and its file, location left to the plan
why: Owns is the boundary a planner checks, and the old line named both auth endpoints by path; the four booking paths are booking-api@v1's Interface, and PRD v2 Team and delivery gives the database to the backend developer, as the invocation says. Naming the Compose file as owned keeps one owner wherever it lives: simple-login.integration owns the root package.json scripts and will start PostgreSQL from them (intake record H18), so a root-level compose file would otherwise sit between two nodes. Where the file goes is the plan's D{n}, routed to H14. A spec for simple-login.integration that claimed root-level infrastructure files would have made me pin the location here.

question: What does simple-login.backend's Isolation strategy say now that bookings live in PostgreSQL 17, in its own file and in the embedded summary?

options.label: real PostgreSQL for booking tests; replay of all three contracts with clock and given; how the test database is started left to the plan
options.consequence: The line keeps app.inject() with the injected clock and random source, adds that tests reading or writing bookings run against a real PostgreSQL 17, never a mock or an in-memory stand-in, extends the replay to booking-api with each fixture's clock and given bookings, and replaces 'no open port needed' with 'the service itself opens no port', since the tests now reach a database. Whether tests use the Compose service's database, a second database or a throwaway container is H14's.

options.label: add only the real-PostgreSQL clause
options.consequence: The literal minimum of the invocation; the line would still say the gate replays only the auth-api and profile-api fixtures, although booking-api@v1's Validation makes its producer replay all 35, and 'no open port needed' would hide the database connection.

options.label: also fix the Compose service as the test database and TZ for the test runs
options.consequence: Settles more at spec level, but the Compose choice decides whether a fixture replay that starts from no bookings erases the bookings a developer made with npm start, and TZ is ADR-002's rule for every node's tests, which the plan applies; both are plan content.

chosen: real PostgreSQL for booking tests; replay of all three contracts with clock and given; how the test database is started left to the plan
why: The invocation requires the real-PostgreSQL sentence (PRD v2 Constraints). booking-api@v1 Validation says the producer's replay sets its injected clock to each fixture's clock and creates the given bookings directly, starting from none, and that the sequence properties (G5, G11, G17) are the producer's own tests on a real PostgreSQL, so the node's isolation now has a database in it and the line says so. Tests that need no booking (sign-in, sessions, the profile) still need no database, so the clause is limited to tests that read or write bookings, as PRD v2 words it. The test database's provenance and TZ are routed to H14 with the routed items carried there.

question: How does simple-login.backend's Overview gain the database, the rooms, the bookings and the time zone, given that it says the service 'answers exactly two endpoints', and how much of the booking design does it state?

options.label: restate the paragraph; state ADR-level facts, leave mechanisms to the plan
options.consequence: The Overview keeps its true sentences (Fastify on Node.js 24 in TypeScript, accounts in memory, scrypt, ADR-001's tokens, the closing contracts sentence with booking-api@v1 added) and gains: the PostgreSQL 17 database this node owns under Docker Compose (Colima on macOS); each account's time zone; the profile with it; the four pre-loaded rooms with their offices' zones; the four booking uses; instants with no zone in the service and the injected clock deciding started and ended (ADR-002); no two bookings of one room overlapping even at the same moment, enforcement left to the plan's D{n}; bookings surviving the restart that still signs users out. 'Exactly two endpoints' goes.

options.label: append a bookings paragraph, edit only the false clause
options.consequence: Smaller diff, but the first paragraph would still describe the accounts without their zones and the closing sentence would list only the auth and profile contracts, so the Overview would read as two specs stacked.

options.label: also state the enforcement and where rooms are stored
options.consequence: An exclusion constraint and rooms as a seeded table would read as settled before H14 weighs them (Q-013 calls the constraint 'one way'), and the spec would become an implementation plan.

chosen: restate the paragraph; state ADR-level facts, leave mechanisms to the plan
why: The invocation names the Overview for the rooms, bookings and their endpoints, the account time zone and the database. 'Answers exactly two endpoints' is false under PRD v2 and booking-api@v1, so the paragraph is restated, not appended to. The facts it adds are those PRD v2 (Constraints, Team and delivery, Demo accounts, Rooms, US-4 to US-6, AC-5.4) and the accepted ADRs fix; the root spec's Decisions put how exactly one of two overlapping bookings wins in this node's D{n} (DEC-077), so the Overview names the rule and not the mechanism. Whether rooms live in code or in a table is not said, because nothing above the plan decides it.

question: The root's child-node table repeats simple-login.backend's old Purpose ('authenticate built-in users and serve the signed-in user's profile over HTTP'). The invocation names only the embedded summary. Is the table's Purpose cell changed too?

options.label: leave the cell; route it to the run
options.consequence: The touch changes only what the invocation names, as the Touch paragraph and the step's done-when require. Until a later step rewrites it, the table describes the backend without booking: incomplete, not false. The orchestrator decides once, for all three children, whether a touch after H9 or the align refreshes the column.

options.label: rewrite the cell to the new Purpose
options.consequence: The root reads consistently at once, but the step edits a line the invocation does not name, and H8 and H9 would face the same choice for their rows, possibly deciding it differently.

chosen: leave the cell; route it to the run
why: hsdd-spec's Touch paragraph: change only what the invocation and the routed items name, the parent's embedded summary only when named. The invocation names the embedded summary, and the root's touch left the child table to hsdd-reconcile for contract versions only (H6), whose version ripple writes Produces, Consumes and Sources there, not Purpose. The table's Purpose column is already a short label rather than a copy (simple-login.web's cell differs from its summary's Purpose), so the old cell stays true for what it names. A consider item to the run lets one decision cover the three rows.
evidence: hsdd-spec SKILL.md Touch and Citation Touch

question: Q-013, Q-017, Q-018 and Q-022 target H14, simple-login.backend's phase-plan-append, and reached this spec touch only because H14's target is the same node; the step must close every routed item, and a closed item no longer reaches H14. How are they closed?

options.label: close each as explained and carry its text to H14
options.consequence: Each is closed 'explained', naming what of it the touched header and Overview now state, and the report routes one item per original to H14 with the same kind and the original text, prefixed by where it came from. H14 still receives Q-017's must-address. H11, the citation touch on the same node, will match the carried items in turn and face the same choice.

options.label: close each as addressed
options.consequence: True only for the few clauses the header and Overview now state (the account time zone, instants, the injected clock, the real PostgreSQL); the rest (the replay rig's clock, given, DELETE and 204, the exclusion constraint's re-read, the title's code points, the failing shipped tests) would vanish from H14 unaddressed.

options.label: leave the consider items open
options.consequence: Keeps them for H14 untouched, and the gate only warns for an unclosed consider item, but the step's done-when requires every routed item in closes, and Q-017 is a must-address the gate refuses to leave open.

chosen: close each as explained and carry its text to H14
why: The Touch paragraph forbids editing the Phase Plan, so this step cannot address plan content, and the step's done-when requires every routed item closed. Carrying the text keeps H14's input whole; the original ids stay in the carried text for the owner's trail. Matching an item on a handoff to every step on that handoff's target (routed.mjs, B-10) is what brings plan items to a spec touch; the orchestrator may prefer to re-open them itself, which is why the report's notes say so.

question: DEC-080's Purpose says the backend serves 'each room's bookings on a date'. Under ADR-002 the web app turns the date into a range and the backend applies no zone. Does Purpose keep the PRD's 'on a date' or say 'in a time range'?

options.label: in a time range
options.consequence: Purpose matches ADR-002 Decision 4 and booking-api@v1's GET /api/rooms (from, to), and the Overview's 'in a requested range'; it no longer echoes PRD v2 US-4's wording.

options.label: on a date, as DEC-080 wrote it
options.consequence: Reads like the user story, but tells a backend planner that the service takes a date, the alternative ADR-002 rejected ('The backend turning a picked date into a range').

why: A node's Purpose states what the node does, and ADR-002 Decision 4 puts the date-to-range conversion in the web app; the backend's input is two instants. This corrects DEC-080's wording in both the file and the embedded summary; the rest of DEC-080 stands.

question: S09 was handed four items on H14 (Q-013, Q-017, Q-018, Q-022) because an item on a handoff id also matches any step on that handoff's target (B-10). It closed them as explained and carried each text to H14 as a new item. Keep that, or rework the step?

options.label: Keep it; log the matching as a finding
options.consequence: The four texts reach H14 as new items with the same kinds (Q-017's copy stays must-address); H11, a step on the same node before H14, will be handed the copies too and has to carry them again.

options.label: Rework S09 to leave the items open
options.consequence: Not possible within the protocol: a step must close every item its dispatch lists, so the rework would end the same way.

chosen: Keep it; log the matching as a finding
why: The step followed its dispatch and lost nothing: each carried text is verbatim and keeps its kind. The churn comes from B-10 matching an item on a handoff to every step on that handoff's node, not only to consistency steps; that is an hsdd-auto defect to fix after the run, not something a step can avoid. A way to make the items wait for H14 would have changed this.

question: S09's report lists reads outside its inputs (the backend's code and package files, earlier step records, the run's scripts). Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: The backend's text stands.

options.label: Rework without those reads
options.consequence: The Owns and Isolation lines would be written without knowing what the shipped service and its tests already do.

why: All reads are inside the repository and serve the node's own text; none is out of bounds. A read outside the repository would have changed this.
